t.E319.agn: TBHQ is authorised in the EU with an acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 0.7 mg/kg body weight. In its detailed exposure assessment in 2016, EFSA stated that in calculations using the maximum permitted levels the ADI could be exceeded in toddlers and children, but that in realistic (refined) scenarios it was not exceeded in any group.
t.E319.body: In rats, 78–88% of orally ingested TBHQ is excreted in the urine, most of it within the first 24 hours; most of that in the urine is conjugated with sulphate and a small part with glucuronic acid. 2–6% is excreted in the faeces; only trace amounts remain in tissues.
t.E319.prod: Produced chemically by reacting hydroquinone with isobutylene or tert-butyl alcohol.
t.E319.regx.0: Refined exposure assessment; ADI 0.7 mg/kg body weight/day, ADI not exceeded in refined scenarios.
t.E319.summary: A petroleum-derived synthetic antioxidant. It delays rancidity in frying oils and fatty snacks.
t.E319.what: It is an antioxidant that delays the oxidation and rancidity of fats.
